dependencies.heard: Central telephone intake and forwarding of support requests
dependencies.quote: Frerk Sievers: IT systems. Cisco telephony: RPO <24 h, RTO 8 h. Protection need: confidentiality medium (call and contact data are internal business data); integrity low (incorrect call data can be recognised and corrected); authenticity low (calls do not have to meet a high standard of proof). Cisco telephony provides the central telephone intake and forwarding of support requests.

dependencies.heard: Ticket system recording, classifying, assigning and tracking support requests
dependencies.quote: Frerk Sievers: IT systems. BMC Remedy AR System: RPO <1 h, RTO 8 h. Protection need: confidentiality medium (tickets hold internal technical and personal details); integrity medium (wrong priorities or status data impair the handling); authenticity medium (whoever created and whoever handled a ticket must be traceable). BMC Remedy AR System records, classifies, assigns and tracks support requests and faults.

dependencies.heard: E-mail, knowledge documents, shift handovers and coordination in support
dependencies.quote: Frerk Sievers: IT systems. Microsoft 365: RPO <1 h, RTO 8 h. Protection need: confidentiality medium (e-mails and files hold internal support information); integrity medium (incorrect information can be corrected from the ticket); authenticity medium (sender and handling must be traceable). Microsoft 365 is used for e-mail, knowledge documents, shift handovers and coordination in support.

dependencies.heard: Substitute ticket system managing service requests and incidents, synchronised with TicketME
dependencies.quote: Frerk Sievers: IT systems. Atlassian Jira Service Management: RPO <1 h, RTO 8 h. Protection need: confidentiality medium (tickets hold internal technical and personal details); integrity medium (priority, status and solution must be documented correctly); authenticity medium (whoever created and whoever handled a ticket must be traceable). Atlassian Jira Service Management manages service requests and incidents and synchronises defined cases with TicketME.

dependencies.heard: Helpdesk staff taking, prioritising, first-analysing and escalating requests
dependencies.quote: Frerk Sievers: Roles. IT helpdesk staff: 10 in normal operation, 4 in emergency operation, needed within 8 h, remote or office. They take requests, prioritise them, carry out first analysis and escalate to the responsible support groups.

conflicts.about: RTO of helpdesk-and-support: the prose says more than 168 hours, the explicit RTO line says 8 h

sides.claim: The prose justification says the RTO is more than 168 hours.
sides.speaker: Frerk Sievers
sides.dropped_quote: Frerk Sievers: The IT helpdesk and support process has an RTO of more than 168 hours, because financial and operational impacts of an outage are to be expected.

sides.claim: The explicit RTO statement gives 8 hours, matching the 8 h RTO of every resource and the 8 h staff availability.
sides.speaker: Frerk Sievers

conflicts.why: The explicit scored line 'RTO: 8 h.' is consistent with all stated system RTOs (8 h) and the 8 h staff need, whereas the prose appears to be a boilerplate sentence contradicting it, so 8 h is carried as stated.

conflicts.about: MTPD: the stated line says >168 h, but the stated operational grid reaches the intolerable level 4 at 24 h, which per the method gives an MTPD of 24 h

sides.claim: The interviewee states the MTPD is beyond the last horizon.
sides.speaker: Frerk Sievers

sides.claim: The stated operational impact row reaches high (4) at 24 h, so under the method's MTPD rule the earliest intolerable horizon is 24 h.
sides.quote: Frerk Sievers: Impact operational: 1 h 1, 2 h 2, 4 h 2, 8 h 3, 24 h 4, 72 h 4, 168 h 4.
sides.speaker: Frerk Sievers

conflicts.why: The method fixes MTPD as the earliest horizon where the worst category reaches threshold 4, and the stated operational row does so at 24 h, so 24 h follows the grid; the manager should confirm at the walk.

gaps.what: The prose RTO justification contradicts the explicit RTO line (8 h vs >168 h), so the reasoning behind 8 h is undocumented.
gaps.ask: Is the RTO of the helpdesk-and-support process really 8 h, and if so what justifies it given the prose speaks of more than 168 hours?

gaps.what: The stated MTPD (>168 h) contradicts the stated operational grid, which reaches the intolerable level 4 at 24 h.
gaps.ask: Do you accept 24 h as the MTPD for helpdesk-and-support, per the grid and the method's MTPD rule, instead of the stated >168 h?

gaps.what: No activity-level RPO was stated; the <1 h proposal rests only on the ticket systems' asset RPOs while telephony is <24 h.
